question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The first equation is a false statement. Hence, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=24 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=10 \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-20\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$, the second equation by $2$, and adding the resulting equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}23{x}_{2} &=92 \\ {x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=10 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4(4) &=10 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=-6 \\ {x}_{1} &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-20 \\ 4(-2)-3(4) &=-20 \\ -20 &=-20\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=4$, which means

$$
-2{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+(4)=2.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -16\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -16\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -16\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -16\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-8 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-16\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-7\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-7$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-7) &=9 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-12 \\ {x}_{1} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=-7$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ 3(6)+5(-7) &=-16 \\ -17 &=-16\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 22\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 22\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=22\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-1) &=-15 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1} &=9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=9$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=22 \\ 3(9)+5(-1) &=22 \\ 22 &=22\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=9$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$, which means

$$
9{a}_{1}-{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(9)+(-1)=8.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=6$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ (6)-{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ {x}_{2} &=7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=7$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=7$, which means

$$
6{c}_{1}+7{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(6)+(7)=13.
$$
